title: ‘Starlog’ Magazine Returns with First Cover in 17 Years
full_text: × Skip to main content By Aaron Couch Plus Icon Aaron Couch Film Editor View All November 3, 2026 8:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Star Log returns with a new cover (right), 50 years after its first issue (left). Starlog The last time there was a new edition of Starlog magazine, J.J. Abrams’ Star Trek was still weeks away from hitting theaters, Robert Downey Jr. was just scratching the surface of Tony Stark’s potential on the set of Iron Man 2 , and George Lucas was still years away from selling Lucasfilm to Disney. In other words, it’s been a minute. But 17 years after publishing its final issue in April 2009, Starlog is back with a new edition, which arrives Nov. 13. The magazine launched in 1976 and gained a fanbase for being one of the few places to get reliable news and interviews about geek culture. It launched with a cover focusing on Star Trek , one of its key areas of expertise, but the magazine’s editors and writers also pioneered coverage of Star Wars . (The new issue chronicles some of the rumors it put out a year before the movie opened). In all, Starlog published 374 issues and more than 25,000 pages. Related Stories Lifestyle GQ Expands Men of the Year Footprint in L.A. Movies Cinemark Won't Screen Brad Pitt's 'Cliff Booth' Movie Over Netflix's Demands, CEO Says The new iteration will publish one issue a year under editor in chief Annalee Newitz, a founding editor of io9 . In addition to the film and TV-focused features Starlog was known for, the new Starlog will also delve into futurism, as the cover from Gabriel Yeganyan highlights. The opening story of issue No. 1 looks at the viability of humans farming crops on planets outside of Earth, for example. “Science fiction and fantasy give us a sandbox to reimagine our world, and Starlog is your invitation to play along,” said Newitz in a statement. “We’re honoring the fannish legacy of the original magazine and bringing it into the future with hopeful, awe-inspiring, and scientifically grounded explorations of where humanity could go next.” Starlog The revival was announced earlier this year, and includes a podcast hosted by Jordan Hoffman, a veteran journalist who has contributed to The Hollywood Reporter , as well as its weekly Lodestar

title: BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’
full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 8:11am PT BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ 45 minutes ago Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Speaking about an editing error that triggered a $10 billion defamation lawsuit pursued by President Donald Trump against the BBC , the broadcaster’s deputy director-general Rhodri Talfan-Davies said Tuesday that “a lot has changed since then.” Talfan-Davies said there were two issues about the BBC’s handling of the controversial episode of investigative show “Panorama.” “One was the actual edit itself, and second, and I think probably more profound in the end, was the BBC’s sluggishness in its response,” he told journalists at a Broadcasting Press Guild lunch. Related Stories Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon 'Chiikawa' Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller 'Paradise Lost' Debuts 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win He outlined the measures that the BBC had implemented to address these issues, which included his own appointment in June 2026. “A lot has changed since then. There’s been a reform of the editorial standards committee, which has been led by Caroline Thomson. The role of the deputy director-general has been created precisely to grip those types of moments and make sure that we get to quick, timely decisions,” he said. He added that the BBC had “instigated over the last 12 months what we call ‘Final Gate’ processes on our most contentious programs.” Explaining what these “Final Gate” processes were, he said, “It means that before you commit to transmission or broadcasting, all the key players involved in the title, including editorial policy, including compliance execs in each of the key genre, they get in the room and they go line by line through the key risks of the program. So there is a really diligent and thorough assessment of the program before it airs.” He cautioned that he couldn’t guarantee that “there won’t be future issues in an organization that digs deep and delivers big investigations … I mean, I’m not naïve.” However, he added, “I do think the processes and controls put in place in the last 12 months put us in a much stronger place.” Talfan Davies, who is a journalist by training, recalled his reaction when he heard of the editing error. “I thought it was a mistake,” he said. Prompted by Variety to expand on that, he said, “Well, I don’t think there was anything malign in it. Right? I think the edit as it stood in the program created a mistaken impression about what precisely was said in that moment by the President, and we caught that issue. It was a BBC review that identified the issue. The real problem was we then didn’t act quickly to put the issue to bed, to be transparent about what had happened, and to apologize for it.” Questioned about whether there was an issue with the culture among BBC journalists that may have caused the editing mistake, he responded, “No, because I think if you look at the wider program, the whole program, you’ll see the extreme care that has been taken in terms of the balance of perspectives and viewpoints in the program. I just think that one edit was problematic.” Asked if he felt it was more likely that the BBC would be able to win the case in the U.S. than six months ago, he said, “Well, I think the key next moment is the decision by the Florida court on whether it has the jurisdiction to even decide this. I think our case on that is very strong, but I’m not in the business of second guessing judges. But we have put our best foot forward in terms of setting out the arguments about why we don’t think it should be heard in a U.S. court, and we’ll wait to hear what the judge says.” Moving onto other issues, Talfan-Davies was asked about accusations of left-wing bias at the BBC by right-wing politicians like Nigel Farage. Talfan-Davies explained what his response would be if Farage were in the room making that accusation. “I’d say two things. Firstly, it’s not my experience at the BBC. I’ve worked in many newsrooms. The discussion is robust, and the conversation is pretty open-minded in terms of different perspectives,” he said. “What I would say is that whilst I don’t see that evidence of bias, you always have to constantly review how you’re doing. “One of the parts of my role is to make sure, as an executive team, we up the ante in terms of how we robustly review our editorial performance. It’s one thing to look at audience metrics, but you also need to really closely scrutinize and be rigorous about how you’re delivering, if you like, your ‘public mission.’ It’s one of the areas that I’m discussing with [the BBC’s director general Matt Brittin], and we’ll say more in the coming months about how we really up the ante on that.” ‘Elsinore,’ ‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’ and ‘Animol’ Lead British Independent Film Awards Nominations Versant Sees Q3 Profit Drop Despite Upticks in Non-TV Operations Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here’s How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free BTS, Katseye Drive Hybe to Record Quarterly Revenue and Profit ‘Okinawa Saudade’ Director Matsubayashi Yoju on a 10-Year Journey Tracing Brazilian Dancers’ Island Roots Loading comments...

title: Russell Brand Trial: Jury Begins Verdict Deliberations
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars View All November 3, 2026 8:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Russell Brand ‘s rape trial has concluded and the jury has begun deliberations on a verdict. After more than three weeks of evidence, the jury will now consider whether to convict or acquit Brand of seven charges: three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one count of attempted indecent assault. The latter was reduced from indecent assault during the trial. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all charges. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Oscars: Every Best Picture Winner Back To The Beginning In 1929 A verdict will not be returned on Tuesday after Judge Mr Justice Bennathan sent the jury home at 4PM local time. He told jurors to “resist talking about the case” until they are all gathered again on Wednesday morning. The judge spent much of the day summarizing the evidence for the jury, going through each charge in detail. This followed closing arguments from the prosecution and defense. Watch on Deadline In legal directions last week, the judge told the jury that they are not under pressure to reach a swift verdict. “No jury can be criticized for taking too little or too much time in their deliberations, you alone must decide on that,” he told them. Bennathan said the jury must reach unanimous verdicts on each of the charges to convict Brand. He reminded jurors last week that the burden of proof is on the prosecution and that Brand is entitled to the benefit of the doubt. In legal directions to the jury last week, Bennathan also told the jury to disregard the 2023 Channel 4 documentary that carried allegations about Brand when coming to their decision. “Do not think that a few women making anonymous complaints in a TV show adds any support at all to the prosecution,” he said at the time. “The defendant denied the allegations [in the documentary] in robust, detailed terms. They were never tested in any court.” Both the prosecution and defense discussed the documentary at length during their closing arguments. Also new to cast are Lonzo Liggins ( Yellowstone ), comedian John Novosad and Denzel Papillon. The eight-episode half-hour addiction-themed dramedy is now in production in Utah starring Craig Ferguson and Megyn Price. The series will be distributed by Angel. Craig Ferguson stars as Nick McTavers and Megyn Price stars as Liza. In Quitters , “after Liza, an upbeat soccer mom, falls into the cycle of opioid addiction, she lands at Unplugged, an unconventional recovery center run by Nick McTavers, a former heavy-metal legend. To put her life back on track, Liza must learn to rely on an eclectic family of patients and counselors who help her navigate the long road of recovery.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series 'Quitters' For Angel News BBC Top Brass "Looking At Options" For Next Phase Of $400 Million Worth Of Savings, Says Deputy DG Lennon will play Brian, Liza’s husband, “caught between love for his family and the limits of what he can endure as her addiction takes hold”. The series is directed by Darrin “Fletch” Fletcher and Chet Thomas and produced through their FletChet Entertainment banner, and was written and created by Dave Parkin. Executive producers include Chet Thomas, Darrin Fletcher, Eric Handler, Chase Vergari, Ibrahim Mohammed, Dave Parkin, Edward Neumeier, Rob Gibbs, HR Brown and Alema Harrington. “This ensemble is everything we hoped for,” said Fletch and Chet. “Every role has been cast with someone who brings real heart and humor to it, on both sides of this story — the recovery center and the families whose lives it touches. Rickards is represented by Alchemy Entertainment, Play Management, and IAG. Handler is represented by 3 Arts Entertainment. Liggins is represented by Love Talent Agency, Susan McCarty Agency, and Outlaw Artist Management. Novosad is represented by Comedy Works Entertainment. Papillon is represented by Love Talent Agency. full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max BBC Top Brass “Looking At Options” For Next Phase Of $400 Million Worth Of Savings, Says Deputy DG New Anti-Harassment Laws Lead To Questions From UK Film & TV Industry John Leeson Dies: Actor Who Voiced Iconic Role In ‘Doctor Who’ Was 83 View All November 3, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Celebrity Traitors' BBC/Studio Lambert The BBC ’s top brass is in the process of “looking at options for the next stage of savings,” according to the Deputy Director General, which will total another £300M ($400M). Rhodri Talfan Davies said it is very unlikely another big savings announcement will come before Christmas but stressed that the “lion’s share” of the cash has to be found before the end of the current BBC charter in 2027/28. He said these conversations are currently taking place at the very upper echelons of the broadcaster. “The executive senior team is now looking at options for the next stage of savings,” Talfan Davies told journalists at a Broadcasting Press Guild lunch. “We haven’t yet shared those with the [wider] team because we’re still working through them. There are lots of ideas on the table, but until the Executive Committee reaches a decision, there’s nothing to announce.” Related Stories News 'Blue Eye Samurai' Sets Season 2 Release Date At Netflix News Jason Statham & Guy Ritchie Reunite For Netflix Feature 'Dogfight' Talfan Davies was interim Director General in April when the BBC announced it was laying off 2,000 people. Since then, his new boss Matt Brittin, the permanent DG, has been busily enacting the £500M savings plan, a tricky task in the funding climate. Around £200M has been found so far. Watch on Deadline Last month, the BBC made the long-awaited announcement that it would be shutting youth-skewing linear network BBC Three along with the BBC Scotland channel and Radio 4 Extra. Our analysis spotlighted how the worst is to come and floated that speculation internally has turned to the future of radio and podcast streamer BBC Sounds. Today, Talfan Davies gave press a window into the corporation’s thinking around Sounds and VoD platform BBC iPlayer, which is in the process of being transformed. “The real question – and I don’t know the answer – is whether iPlayer will be more and more the home for some of our biggest audio brands,” he speculated. “But you’ll still need a strongly creative collection of all your services. Brands come and go, but there will be a home for BBC audio content and its listeners.” The BBC remains unsure over its future funding model as charter negotiations with the government continue and Talfan Davies said the corporation is in the meantime having to “ride two horses in terms of financial outcomes, which is not ideal.” The main funding solution to have emerged so far appears to be the so-called “ Netflix tax,” which would force streaming service subs to pay the £180 annual license fee as it desperately tries to get more audiences to pay the fee. With Netflix in a tight spot having just laid off 1,000 staff itself, Talfan Davies acknowledged that the streamers “might not be supportive” of the proposal but said “in some ways it’s not a million miles” from yesteryear. He was referring to a time when audiences in the UK had to pay the fee even if they only watched other linear TV channels. “There are echoes of that reform in what has been suggested,” said Talfan Davies. Case against Donald Trump “very strong” Donald Trump Photo by Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images On the day of the U.S. midterms, and with Republicans expected to be inflicted with heavy defeats, Talfan Davies addressed the $10B defamation lawsuit the BBC faces from Donald Trump. While saying he is “not in the business of second-guessing judges,” Talfan Davies said the BBC’s case to have the defamation suit thrown out of a Florida court over jurisdiction is “very strong.” “We’ve put our best foot forward in setting out the arguments about why we don’t think it should be heard in the U.S. at all,” he said. “I would like the judge to agree.” The situation emerged when a BBC Panorama show made a botched edit of Trump’s Jan. 6 speech that appeared to show him inciting insurrection. Talfan Davies, who as Deputy DG now oversees the editorial standards and legal teams, said “a lot has changed” internally since the error was made and the “sluggishness” of the BBC’s response was “probably more profound” than the error with the package itself. He stressed the BBC has introduced “‘before final gate’ processes for our most contentious programmes” that sees key people involved “go through a programme line by line.” He caveatted by saying “anyone in my job who says there won’t be future issues in an organization is being naive.” “The BBC does big investigations,” he added. “I’m not naive about that. title: GQ Expands Men of the Year Footprint in L.A.
full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Adam Baidawi attends the GQ Men of the Year Awards at London's 180 Thames on Nov. 18, 2025. (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) GQ ‘s Men of the Year footprint in Los Angeles is growing — with some A-list names in tow. A marquee franchise for the Condé Nast publication, Men of the Year will be celebrated at three events this month in a showing that will mark the mag’s most ambitious run in the annual rollout. And this time it’s being steered by global editorial director Adam Baidawi, who took over in February 2026 after longtime editor Will Welch departed for a role working for Pharrell Williams in Paris. GQ has drafted Chris Rock , Andrew Garfield and Matt Damon to serve as Men of the Year co-hosts for their respective work in Misty Green, Artificial and The Odyssey . The three cover stars will bring some star power to the 31st installment of the series, which will also feature fellow honorees like GQ’s director of the year Denis Villeneuve for Dune: Part Three and designer of the year Michael Rider of Celine. Related Stories Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards Lifestyle Bob Iger Stresses Value of Communal Cultural Experiences in World "Rife With Disruption and Polarization" at PAC NYC Icons of Culture Gala As for those events, the Men of the Year celebration kicks off Nov. 10 at the recently opened Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, where GQ will host Villeneuve with a champagne reception, a live recording of GQ’s “One More Question” interview series fronted by senior special projects editor Zach Baron and a VIP screening of Dune: Part Two ahead of the franchise’s final bow on Dec. 18. Next up will be a “Breakouts” house party at the Sheats-Goldstein Residence on Nov. 11. The soiree wil host and toast the mag’s 13 Breakouts of 2026, a roster of boldfaced names across film, TV, music, comedy and podcasting. (The list will be published on GQ.com on Nov. 9.) And last but not least: the anticipated Men of the Year bash will return to Chateau Marmont on Nov. 12. An intimate dinner honoring the GQ’s cover stars will open the night and feature some starry (and filmed) toasts from special guests who will fete their friends. Then, after dessert, the action turns up a notch for the annual Men of the Year party that will once again host VIPs across entertainment, fashion, sports and culture. “This year’s GQ Men of the Year honorees have delivered extraordinary performances and propelled the cultural conversation of 2026. We wanted to meet that creative ambition with some of our own. Expanding to three events in Los Angeles — something brand new to Men of the Year — gives us the space to celebrate their work, get into the ideas behind it and introduce the talent we think everyone needs to watch next. It’s an ambitious new chapter for a tradition we love,” Baidawi tells The Hollywood Reporter in a statement. THR

title: Funko Launches New ‘Harry Potter’ Mystery Collectibles Ahead of HBO Series
full_text: As HBO prepares to bring audiences back to Hogwarts this Christmas, Funko is getting in on the magic with a new collection of “Harry Potter” mystery figures , including a chance to uncover an ultra-rare collectible. The new “Harry Potter” POP! Mystery collection features six characters from the original film series: Harry Potter , Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley, Luna Lovegood and twins Fred and George Weasley. Each four-inch vinyl figure comes in blind-box packaging, meaning buyers won’t know which character they’ve received until they open it. Each box also includes a corresponding collectible POP! card. Mystery Box SHOP ONLINE $14.99 Priced at $14.99 each, the figures have equal one-in-six odds of appearing in a standard box. The release is part of Funko’s recently introduced POP! Mystery line, which taps into the growing popularity of blind-box collectibles. The first season will adapt “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” with Francesca Gardiner serving as showrunner and executive producer and Mark Mylod directing multiple episodes. HBO is already developing a second season based on “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” with Kit Harington recently announced as Gilderoy Lockhart. The HBO adaptation marks the franchise’s first major live-action television retelling, more than two decades after Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint first brought the central trio to the big screen. title: Nicole Taylor, Country Singer in Triplet Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35
full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:58am PT Nicole Taylor, Country Singer in Triplet Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35 By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Funko Launches New ‘Harry Potter’ Mystery Collectibles Ahead of HBO Series 31 minutes ago Nicole Taylor, Country Singer in Triplet Trio Taylor Red, Dies at 35 32 minutes ago Josh O’Connor Describes Bond Rumors as ‘Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment’: ‘To Be Considered Is Extraordinary’ 1 hour ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nicole Taylor , a country singer and one-third of the identical triplet trio Taylor Red , which built a massive following on TikTok and Youtube, has died after a battle with breast cancer. She was 35. Taylor died Sept. 28 at her home in Nashville, Tenn., according to a statement on the group’s website. Her sisters and bandmates, Nika and Natalie Taylor, announced her death in an emotional video posted Monday, Nov. 2. Related Stories Box Office: 'Street Fighter' Aims for $30 Million Opening, 'You Can See Everything' Could Score $8 Million Start Box Office: ‘Clayface’ Lands at No. 1 with $10.4 Million Debut, ‘You Can See Everything’ Adds $6.14 Million on Friday “We are heartbroken to announce the passing of our sister Nicole Taylor,” Nika said in the video. “We honestly thought she’d be healed here on earth, but now she’s healed in heaven.” Nicole was diagnosed with an aggressive form of stage 3 breast cancer in 2022. Although she initially responded well to chemotherapy and was declared to have no evidence of disease, the cancer eventually returned and progressed to stage 4. Doctors gave her three months to live following the diagnosis, but she lived for another year. “She tried not to live in fear, remained really hopeful,” Natalie said. “She traveled, she tried to live life, she worked really hard, she tried to have fun.” Born and raised in southern Mississippi, Nicole formed Taylor Red with her identical triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie. The siblings began performing together in 2010 under the name Red Roots, releasing three albums before rebranding as Taylor Red in 2018. Known for their genre-blending country music and tight harmonies, the sisters played guitar, banjo, fiddle and mandolin. The trio later found a new audience on social media, where their synchronized performances, musical covers and comedy bits helped them amass millions of followers. In 2020, Variety featured Taylor Red in a report examining how female country and pop groups were using TikTok to build audiences outside traditional industry channels, alongside acts like Avenue Beat and Four Diamonds. Their 2021 song “Country Money” became one of their best-known releases. In their tribute, Nika and Natalie remembered Nicole, the oldest member of her sisters by minutes, as their “fearless leader” and best friend. “Nicole, the oldest of us three sisters, will be greatly missed,” they wrote on the group’s website. “She was our leader and our best friend. We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again.” The sisters said Nicole remained devoted to her Christian faith throughout her illness, continuing her exercise, travel and work even while undergoing treatment. The family has held a private funeral service. In lieu of flowers, fans are encouraged to make donations in Nicole’s memory to Samaritan’s Purse, one of her favorite charities. title: Cinemark Won’t Screen Brad Pitt’s ‘Cliff Booth’ Movie Over Netflix’s Demands, CEO Says
full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:58am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Brad Pitt in Netflix's 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' Netflix Two theater chains are refusing to screen the upcoming sequel to Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood . Cinemark and Regal have decided against giving any of their Imax screens to The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , which has Brad Pitt reprising his role as a fearless stuntman in a movie written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. The decision effectively makes Cliff Booth exclusive to AMC among the major chains. During Cinemark’s third-quarter earnings call early Tuesday, CEO Sean Gamble explained that the company decided against running the film due to Netflix ‘s very short release window — which ends just two weeks before the title shifts to streaming — and not wanting to establish a precedent that could come back to haunt the chain in future negotiations. “The Cliff Booth situation is an interesting one,” Gamble said. “We book all of our films on a case-by-case situation. In that particular situation, we always look at things through a long-term lens and how certain precedents and things we might do could affect longer-term industry dynamics. In this particular case, we don’t believe the proposed release model is constructive for the broader theatrical ecosystem, and it’s not aligned [with] what’s of the greatest interest in our theaters.” Gamble also added that keeping The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on its Imax screens during Thanksgiving is a sold play due to the film’s strong advance sales. Cliff Booth will debut in theaters on Nov. 25, then hit Netflix on Dec. 23. For Netflix, which has traditionally resisted filmmakers’ efforts to secure theatrical releases for their movies, the film actually represents a first — the first time the streamer has released a movie in Imax. The slot was originally supposed to go to Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew , but the movie was pushed to February, where it will have a far more generous seven-week theatrical window. Cinemark Holdings posted higher revenue and earnings compared to a year ago, seeing total revenue rise to $1.05 billion versus $857.5 million in the same period of 2025. Gamble predicted the theatrical window could actually widen despite the rise of streaming. “We’re going to continue to see [the window] grow, especially since the commitments were a minimum of 45 days and beyond that many of the larger films continue to have windows of 60-plus days,” he said. “As we turn the corner into 2027, we’re going to see that window continue to expand a bit, especially as additional studios join in.” Etan Vlessing contributed to this report . title: Josh O’Connor Calls Bond Speculation “Incredibly Bizarre Pinch Me Moment”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:51am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Josh O'Connor for 'Disclosure Day' press in 2026 Courtesy of Getty Logo text Josh O’Connor is the latest star to play coy on the reports — including those from The Hollywood Reporter — that he is in the running for the role of James Bond . The Crown , Knives Out and Challengers actor was said to be screen-testing to replace Daniel Craig as Ian Fleming’s iconic MI6 agent. Among the small group of actors also in contention are Callum Turner and Jack Lowden . The Scottish Slow Horses star weighed in just this week on the speculation , telling British GQ : “Oh, Christ… It’s all very flattering. It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise.” Related Stories Movies Pierce Brosnan Supports Callum Turner Being Cast as James Bond: "So Strong..." General News British Celebrity Loses Legal Bid to Prevent Publication of Identity and Sexual Misconduct Allegations The 36-year-old O’Connor, who also led Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day earlier this year, was opening the new Everyman Theatre in his hometown of Cheltenham, England, on Tuesday. He was probed about the Bond reports and admitted: “To be considered in that same sort of bracket is extraordinary.” He described the news as “such an incredibly bizarre pinch me moment… even being uttered in that same sentence and being considered for something like that. But I am afraid,” he continued, “there is nothing to say beyond that.” Toward the end of October, THR heard word that screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios’ James Bond film, directed by Dune ‘s Denis Villeneuve and written by Peaky Blinders mastermind Steven Knight, would be taking place in London imminently. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.” Nina Gold, the woman who cast Lowden in his Emmy-nominated role as Slow Horse ‘s River Cartwright, is also leading the search for Craig’s successor. She also happened to cast O’Connor in his breakout role (as Prince Charles in The Crown ). We await further news. Callum Turner, over to you… THR

title: Should California Subsidize Noah Wyle’s ‘The Pitt’ Pay?
full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho , Katie Kilkenny November 3, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Noah Wyle in 'The Pitt' season three. Warrick Page/HBO Max For nearly 20 years, California has drawn a line between subsidizing pay for people in front of the camera and the workforce behind it. When the state started writing checks to Hollywood in 2009, the thinking was that the purpose of tax credits for films and TV shows would be to create jobs and juice the overall economy. That hasn’t changed through four iterations of the program across three governors. Its refusal to offset a production’s salary for, say, Tom Cruise, has made it an outlier among the 39 states that offer production incentives and is probably the biggest reason why it’s losing its grip as the filming capital of the world. Now — in a major pivot from its historic position that allowing productions to count so-called “above-the-line” spending toward expenditures for filming subsidies would be irresponsible — California is doing the math. Select lawmakers have come to a not-so-surprising conclusion among industry insiders: the state can no longer afford not to. “We’re still not competitive,” says Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur, a key legislator who has been working with Hollywood proponents to fine-tune the state’s incentive program. The idiosyncrasy to California’s film and TV tax credit program has been leveraged by competing states and foreign countries to coax productions into leaving. Now, Gov. Gavin Newsom is trying to fight back. On Monday, Newsom announced another major expansion to the program that, if passed, would increase the annual credit from $750 million to $1 billion and allow a portion of pay for actors, directors and producers to qualify, among other changes. Supporters have been clamoring for these costs to be counted for years, arguing that drastic changes must immediately be implemented to rescue production in California. Despite a record number of titles getting tax credits, production levels in Los Angeles, a barometer of shooting levels in the state, have continued to drop the last two quarters. The region saw a nearly 5 percent decrease in shoot days from June to September compared to the same period last year and an 11 percent drop compared to the previous quarter, according to the latest report from permitting office FilmLA issued last month. The total is 36 percent below the five-year average, highlighting the fierce competition between states and other countries to host Hollywood. Economists, however, remain skeptical about the value of filming subsidies, particularly whether they generate enough jobs and business activity to justify the cost. The Legislative Analyst’s Office said last year that the tax credits indeed increased production activity but that there’s weak evidence indicating that it benefits the state’s overall economy. The latest changes announced on Monday could throw more fuel onto the fire of whether taxpayers should be footing the bill for studios, some of which are engaged in major layoffs even as executive compensation remains sky high. Those same studios, it should be noted, have made a choice to go elsewhere, chasing cost savings. Take the example of the HBO Max hit The Pitt , which actually does shoot in California, on the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank. California is projected to give Parallax TV Productions, whose parent is Warner Bros. Discovery, nearly $49 million in subsidies across the series so far for shooting the show in-state. More than half of that figure will come for the filming of season three, after former Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav saw his total pay package soar to $165 million for 2025 and exit the company with more than half a billion dollars from the studio’s merger with Paramount. Additional layoffs are underway at the combined company, which made just 15 movies combined that filmed in the country over the last two years. While there haven’t been substantive discussions on the issue, Zbur says talks so far have acknowledged that taxpayers shouldn’t be subsidizing compensation for executives or A-listers. He draws a distinction between those two groups and other talent, several of whom he says are “barely getting by and only make family-supporting incomes.” It’s unclear how legislation could be drafted to account for that distinction, though something like a hard cap on individual salaries could be feasible. “There’s been some amount of consensus that we don’t want to allow tax credits for studio executives who are making a lot of money or star actors,” Zbur says. For years, New York, like California, had reservations about subsidies for above-the-line expenditures. But in a major expansion of the program last year, it eliminated a $500,000 cap on those costs. It’s a significant reason why California is poised to lose its title as the filming capital of the world, with New York drawing big-name titles at a much faster pace, according to industry tracker ProdPro’s latest quarterly snapshot, which noted that the state saw a 87 percent increase in production spend in the quarter compared with California’s 17 percent uptick. For California, the change is mainly aimed at drawing big-budget TV shows back to the state, where production in the category is roughly half below historical norms. Across its run, TV titles can accumulate substantial above-the-line costs since they employ a recurring cast, multiple writers, showrunners and producers in a single season. “The competitive reality is clear,” says Stephen G. Weizenecker, a partner at Barnes & Thornburg who handles tax incentives and financing for productions. “States trying to maximize production spending have included above-the-line costs to win the biggest films and television series. By excluding these costs, California has effectively been offering a smaller credit on the productions that it most wants to keep.” Still, questions will inevitably be asked about whether California taxpayers are on the losing side of the bargain. Hawaii in 2024 issued 32 productions $38 million in tax credits, according to a state economic report . Those titles paid $112 million in total wages, the report said, with above-the-line pay accounting for roughly $36.3 million. But just $11.7 million of that went to Hawaii residents; the remaining $24.6 million went to workers outside the state. The figures suggest that expanding tax credit eligibility to cover talent compensation could direct a substantial share of subsidies toward talent who don’t live in the state, raising questions about how much of that spending ultimately benefits the local economy. A major talking point will likely also revolve around California helping pay star salaries for productions that would’ve shot here regardless of the change. Take The Pitt again: If the series was already going to film in California for future seasons, the state will effectively be subsidizing an expense that didn’t influence the production’s location decision. The show already saw the size of its credit nearly double for the third season. Now, it’s probably in line to get even more. And with Newsom leaving office in the new year, it’s an open question on whether his successor in Sacramento will have the same enthusiasm for supercharging the state’s Hollywood tax credit. Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra has been cautious and specific about how he would deploy tax credits if elected. He’s favored expansion based on an “ongoing assessment of where we are losing work: post-production and VFX, independent productions, episodic television at scale, and whatever gaps the data reveals” — in other words, he wants to increase the tax credit, but carefully, and based on specific data. Meanwhile, he has not mentioned above-the-line costs. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to a spokesperson for Becerra on Newsom’s announcement. His rival, Republican Steve Hilton , on the other hand, clearly wants a major tax credit boost. In a move that’s even more aggressive than Newsom’s, he’s called for California to uncap its Hollywood tax credit entirely and include above-the-line costs as eligible expenses. (But, it’s worth noting, as of this writing, Hilton lags behind Becerra in several polls.) Regardless of which candidate wins the governorship, such legislation would face difficult questions in Sacramento, especially at a time when the state is still reeling from federal funding cuts. The optics of including above-the-line costs in a $1 billion annual tax credit fund during a period of serious affordability concerns would be, to say the least, tricky. Any legislators carrying such a bill would need to convince their colleagues in multiple parts of the state where Hollywood has less sway of the wisdom of such a move. But it’s clear that something needs to change to bring production back to Hollywood’s historic home. Could including above-the-line costs in incentives lure sets back? While not being able to do so previously is one of a much larger patchwork of complaints that producers tend to reel off about shooting in L.A., supporters seem to be suggesting that at this point it’s worth trying anything feasible to curb the flight of production. “We’ve made important progress but we can’t rest on our laurels,” Zbur says. “We need to continue focusing on the tax credit program to make sure we’re truly competitive.” THR

title: Indie Outfit Catalytic Films To Launch At AFM With Four-Feature Slate Including James Franco Title ‘Something’s In There’
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Indie Outfit Catalytic Films To Launch At AFM With Four-Feature Slate Including James Franco Title ‘Something’s In There’ Jason Statham & Guy Ritchie Reunite For Netflix Feature ‘Dogfight’ British Independent Film Awards: ‘Elsinore’ Leads Nominations View All November 3, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Catalytic Films EXCLUSIVE: Milena Rimassa will launch Catalytic Films , an independent production, financing, and sales company, at the 2026 American Film Market with a four-feature sales slate, including Something’s In There, starring James Franco. Something’s In There was written and directed by Joel Harber. The film is described as a supernatural horror thriller. It also stars Peter Gold and Elsie Hewitt, with Raoul Max Trujillo ( Apocalypto ), Rob Moran, Paul Ben-Victor, Jayson Warner Smith ( The Walking Dead ), and Alexander Kane. Synopsis reads: Aspiring filmmaker Billy Hobbs takes a night-watchman job at a film studio, where strange sights, sounds, and deaths blur the line between his favorite horror films and reality. He must uncover what is happening before becoming the next victim. Related Stories News Lucky Number Unveils First Image Of Hiam Abbass In Psychological Thriller 'Daughter Of Eden' - AFM Casting Jeremy Renner & Josh Brolin Set For Orlando von Einsiedel's 'A Speck In The Sea'; 193 Launching Sales At AFM The other Catalytic Films titles are: Watch on Deadline Boundaries — Directed by Kirandeep Karnati, the uplifting ensemble drama follows predominantly South Asian women in suburban California who form a cricket team. Challenging cultural expectations and personal limitations, they discover friendship, independence, and solidarity through sport. Paper Flowers — Directed by Mahesh Pailoor (Brahmin Bulls) and produced by Asit Vyas (Zara Si Bhool), the inspirational drama follows USC graduate Shalin Shah, who leaves his Indian American family and Taiwanese American girlfriend to volunteer with the Peace Corps. A rare cancer diagnosis forces him home, where he finds new meaning in love, gratitude, and the time he has left. Kapil Talwalkar (Night Court), Olivia Liang (Kung Fu), Karan Soni (Deadpool), Tom Everett Scott (That Thing You Do!), Faran Tahir (Iron Man) and Meera Simhan (Four Samosas) star. The film earned recognition at Palm Springs, San Luis Obispo, Sedona, and Chandler film festivals. North American viewers can watch Paper Flowers on the Angel Studios streaming service. Catalytic Films is licensing the remaining worldwide rights. We Are Never Alone — Directed and scored by Michel Pascal and produced by Stephen Powers, the docudrama explores human connection, spirituality and music through stories of healing and hope, featuring Michael Beckwith, Gabriella Wright and Temple Hayes. title: Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:24am PT Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada’s Bitcoin Creator Movie ‘Satoshi’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE) By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest ‘Thirteen in Gaza’ Acquired by Koudéta Films for France Ahead of Doha Film Festival 3 hours ago John Travolta Set for Torino Film Festival Award Ahead of ‘Propeller One-Way Night Coach’ Screening (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago First Vatican-Produced Film Submitted to Oscars Boarded by Hollywood Ventures Group (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty/Biscuit Media A new feature film titled “Satoshi,” about Bitcoin’s pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto, is set to be directed by Jason Zada (“The Forest, “Terrarium”) with backing from former NBA champion and tech investor Tristan Thompson . The plan is to start shooting in Saudi Arabia and Los Angeles in spring 2027. Tristan Thompson — who is known in the tabloids for sharing two children with Khloé Kardashian — will produce “Satoshi” alongside Enderby Entertainment principals Rick Dugdale and Dan Petrie Jr. Related Stories How 'You Can See Everything' Became a Surprise Box Office Hit (and Likely One of the Biggest Docs of All Time) Box Office: 'You Can See Everything' Beats 'Clayface' for No. 1 With $11.4 Million in Sleepy Halloween Weekend “Satoshi” is among the first projects under a multi-picture deal between Enderby Entertainment and Saudi Arabia’s Yellow Camel Studios production company. The plan is to shoot the film at JAX Film Studios, a state-of-the-art production complex in the Saudi capital city of Riyadh. The creator of Bitcoin, whose identity and invention remain secret, is also the subject of the Doug Liman-directed film “Bitcoin” (aka “Killing Satoshi”) which has a cast including Casey Affleck, Pete Davidson, Gal Gadot and Isla Fisher. “Bitcoin,” which is currently in post, has sparked controversy for using AI to create the movie’s sets and lighting, having been reportedly filmed in just 20 days inside a “gray box” studio in London. Also on board “Satoshi” as producers are BDE Ventures founder and Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies pioneer Brian D. Evans, as well as actors Aaron Arnold (“Splitting Image”) and Austin Arnold (“Splitting Image,” “Altcoin Daily”), according to a statement from Enderby Entertainment. “Satoshi” will examine the origins of Bitcoin, which was created in 2008 in the wake of the global financial crisis as a way to circumvent traditional financial institutions. Zada and Nate Atkins (“Take This Lollipop”) partnered on the shooting script, based on an original screenplay by Cam Cannon (“Zero Contact”). Zada, who is the founder of the AI-native studio Secret Level, is currently in production on the AI hybrid horror feature “Terrarium.” However, while AI will be used as a tool in making “Satoshi,” AI is “not the main focus of how the film will be made,” according to a rep for the film. “This is a traditional film production, including on-location filming, etc.,” the rep stated. The “Satoshi” logline reads: “A troubled FBI agent partners with a charismatic defense attorney under federal pressure to unmask Bitcoin’s elusive creator, Satoshi Nakamoto — plunging into a high-stakes crypto thriller of government overreach, personal demons, and a mystery that still defies the world.” “Bitcoin wasn’t born in a boardroom. It was released as open-source code by someone who chose to disappear,” Dugdale said in a statement. referring to the ongoing effort to unmask the mysterious Satoshi Nakamoto, author of the bitcoin white paper which laid the theoretical foundations for modern digital currencies. “We’re not interested in a sanitized version of that story,” he added. “We’re bringing in people who understand the code, the culture and why it mattered from the beginning.” “Jason has been pushing the edges of how films get made, and with the support of the Saudi kingdom we have the room to do this properly,” the “Satoshi” producer continued. Commented Thompson: “We are entering a new financial era where money moves at the speed of the internet, value flows seamlessly across borders and entirely new systems of ownership and exchange are emerging. Satoshi sparked a movement that is fundamentally reshaping how the world thinks about wealth, freedom and financial power.” Evans underlined that “for years, the traditional media has misunderstood Bitcoin and the people who built it,” and pointed out that this film “isn’t about unmasking Satoshi. It’s about getting the narrative and story right for the world to finally see.” Enderby Entertainment was founded in 2006 and has previously produced “Blackway,” starring Anthony Hopkins, Julia Stiles and Ray Liotta, which premiered at Venice in 2015; Ben Kingsley-starrer “An Ordinary Man”; “Night Hunter Henry” with Henry Cavill, Ben Kingsley and Alexandra Daddario; and the three-film anthology based on Swedish writer Hakan Nesser’s “Intrigo” trilogy of novels. Zada is repped by UTA and Dante DeSario at Collage. title: Pierce Brosnan Supports Callum Turner Being Cast as James Bond: “So Strong…”
full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Pierce Brosnan in 1995's 'Goldeneye.' United Artists/courtesy Everett Collection Logo text Former James Bond star Pierce Brosnan gave an enthusiastic shout-out to Callum Turner in his quest to become the next 007. During an interview with Vanity Fair , Brosnan was asked about the current “conversation” around the subject of Bond — presumably referring to media coverage about the actors reportedly being tested to take over the iconic role. The MobLand actor was very diplomatic in his answer, generously praising the field of young stars who are up for the part. Related Stories Movies Jack Lowden Is Tight-Lipped on Those Bond Rumors: "I'm Not Going to Add to the Noise" Movies Lowden, Turner or a Dark Horse: One James Bond Casting Test Has Nothing to Do With Acting Yet he did give a particular hat tip to Turner, whom he worked with on the 2017 film The Only Living Boy in New York . “Oh, I’m just an audience member now,” he said. “I’m just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history. All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men. Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.” Brosnan also had praise for Dune director Denis Villeneuve helming the new Bond film. “I think we are going to be blown away,” he said. “[Villeneuve] is such an iconoclastic director. His work is visionary, and his stealth and imagination of camera work and storytelling is so visceral and sensuous. It’s going to be great. It’s going to be truly magnificent.” As reported by The Hollywood Reporter , the actors testing for Bond include Turner and Slow Horses star Jack Lowden. Going into last weekend when auditions were set to take place, Lowden was the favorite in prediction markets. Since then, for whatever reason, Turner has surged ahead. Lowden recently reacted to his Horses co-star, Gary Oldman, suggesting the actor would get the role. “It’s all very flattering,” Lowden said to British GQ . “It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise. It’s very nice, and Gary’s a sweetheart — it’s particularly lovely, coming from someone like him. But I don’t really listen to it.” Previously, Brosnan reacted to his MobLand co-star Helen Mirren blasting the Bond franchise for being sexist, noting, “She let them have it” and admitted, “Yes, there’s a certain agreement there. But there’s a certain world and room to move within the proscenium arch of what [Bond creator and author] Ian Fleming put down. So there’s always going to be conflict.” Mirren had said of the decades-old franchise, “I never liked James Bond. I never liked the way women were in James Bond. The whole concept of James Bond is drenched and born out of profound sexism.” Villeneuve is directing the new Bond outing, with Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing and overseeing the franchise for Amazon MGM Studios, which bought out the creative rights from the Broccoli family in February 2025. title: Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars
full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 7:20am PT Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars 1 hour ago Versant CEO: MS NOW Not Suffering From ‘News Fatigue’ Like Fox News 2 hours ago Versant Sees Q3 Profit Drop Despite Upticks in Non-TV Operations 5 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rose Wong for Variety Scott MacFarlane has traded in the desk once sat behind at CBS News on Election Night for something more direct — livestreamed midterms coverage for the progressive outlet MeidasTouch. He won’t have someone manipulating a Magic Wall or Big Board. He won’t be introduced by swelling orchestral music. And he won’t be competing with colleagues for precious minutes of airtime. MacFarlane will be ready to talk to followers via streaming channels starting at 7 p.m. Tuesday. Related Stories Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon 'Chiikawa' Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller 'Paradise Lost' Debuts Box Office: ‘Street Fighter’ Scores $13 Million Debut as ‘You Can See Everything’ Opens at No. 2 With $5.5 Million on Friday At a traditional TV outlet, says MacFarlane, his contribution would have been curated by producers. This year, he says, “the voice we get to use is my voice. I am going unscripted, without a teleprompter, just telling people point blank what’s happening.” Dozens of independent journalists will do the same. Coverage of returns on Election Night has long been dominated by the nation’s big TV-news outlets . This year, however, so-called “ creators ” — indie journalists and non-traditional experts — want their own piece of the audience. In addition to the MeidasTouch stream, which will feature MacFarlane along with former MSNBC host Katie Phang, former NBC News political guru Chuck Todd will hold forth with colleague Chris Cillizza in a live stream they call “The Projection.” It will appear across YouTube, X, Substack, Decision Desk HQ’s Votes portal and Noosphere, one of many new subscription platforms that offers access to the work of expert journalists. Piers Morgan , whose Uncensored company won millions in funding late last yea r, is traveling from London to host several nights of coverage in the nation’s capital. Jim Acosta and Katie Couric , two popular former mainstream TV anchors, will team up to host a live stream from the University of Virginia, and have booked guests including Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Tara Setmayer. Don Lemon, the former CNN anchor, will greet guests such as Joy Reid and Hunter Biden while presiding over a show in a New York City bar. Even staid CSPAN is getting in on the craze, and plans to simulcast hours of coverage from progressive outlet The Young Turks and conservative commentator Patrick Bet-David. Despite some of the hosts’ mainstream roots, many of them think they can bring viewers something the legacy outlets cannot. “This will be Murdoch-Ellison-free coverage,” says Acosta of the show he and Couric plan to put on, making a direct nod to the ownership of Fox News by the Murdoch family and the control over CBS News and CNN now enjoyed by the Ellison family , which controls the newly formed Skydance. “Katie and I are free to let it rip.” The ability to speak frankly and with little corporate oversight isn’t the main reason pundits and independents are gathering. Many of these people see a big opportunity to generate subscriptions, advertising and revenue — and to draw bigger audiences to their various outlets in an era when the economics of media are decidedly in flux. “I think this is a precursor to what we are going to see in two years, with more audiences coming to platforms like ours, along with more top-tier guests, and more newsmakers,” says Rashida Jones, who was named CEO of Morgan’s company in March after a stint running MSNBC. Advertisers were eager to sponsor Morgan’s shows from Washington, D.C., she says. A good Election Night showing by Morgan, she says, can only generate new audiences and business. Will there be enough of both to help all these companies thrive? About 58% of U.S. adults see social media as a key means of staying current with the news cycle, according to a recent Pew Research Center survey. Approximately 13% indicated social media was the most important way to get news. When Pew issued a similar survey in 2022, 43% of Americans said social media was an important way they got news, and 5% said it was the most important. “The crowd’s going to keep on growing,” says Jones. “This is the turning of the corner of that audience coming to digital-first platforms.” The independents aren’t the only ones who see a growing opportunity. Mainstream media is also seeding the ground. Fox Nation, the Fox News streaming outlet, will run a three-hour live special led by the team behind the popular Ruthless podcast . Josh Holmes, one of the co-hosts, says he will likely not drink alcohol even though the event will take place in front of a crowd in a Washington D.C. bar. “We will try to keep a sense of humor about topics that people often get sort of negative about, and then we always provide what we think is an under-the-hood look at serious topics,” says Holmes. The team doesn’t see the livestream as competing with Fox News coverage led by Bret Baier, Martha MacCallum and Bill Hemmer, says Holmes. “Wwe are supplementing that, trying to give some perspective.” Several “Ruthless” members have jobs as strategic political advisers and can offer unique insights. NBC News this year is launching its first vertical-video program, led by anchor and correspondent Gadi Schwartz. He will be on the ground in Texas and will talk with various NBC News journalists based in different parts of the country. The program will “really look at a more conversational approach to how the night is unfolding,” says Catherine Kim, NBC News’ executive vice president of editorial, and will play out not only on the company’s social media feeds, but also Schwartz’ own. Independents who once had a strong foothold in legacy media may have the best chance of surviving. Couric and Acosta booked their own guests and are taking a strong hand in designing the look and feel of their Election Night program. “We both worked for a long time with legacy media, and I think it made the transition to a digital platform much easier for us, because we came in with a built-in audience to a certain extent,” says Couric. “We want to have both of our audiences intersect and come together on Election Night, and it will be hopefully good for both of us.”’ The duo say they know which elements of news presentation to keep and which to jettison. Delivering important information is in. Doing it in an overly formal way is not. “We want to make it unlike what the networks are doing,” says Acosta. “We are not going to be overly stilted and scripted and all of that stuff. This is much more freewheeling.” And, potentially, blunt. Couric says she can say things that NBC and CBS would never have allowed her to state when she worked for them on programs like “Today” and the “CBS Evening News.” “I think we are liberated,” says Couric. “I don’t think our hands are tied in the way that network anchors are with their corporate overlords breathing down their necks.” And since the program will be done on their own terms, Couric and Acosta can also relax — well, at least a little bit. “We are going to be much more casually dressed than I was when I did election coverage for CBS,” says Couric. “There might be an open bar,” says Acosta. ‘Thirteen in Gaza’ Acquired by Koudéta Films for France Ahead of Doha Film Festival New Japanese Animation Prize Named Nippon Anime Awards, Sets First Ceremony for November 2027 MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here’s How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free Elena Maganini, Film Editor on ‘Dexter,’ ‘Henry, Portrait of a Serial Killer,’ Dies at 70 Emraan Hashmi’s Musical Horror Film ‘Rooh’ Adds Tips Films and Tips Music (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Vote for America 2026:’ Here’s How to Watch Newsmax’s Midterm Election Special Online for Free Loading comments...

title: British Celebrity Loses Legal Bid to Prevent Publication of Identity and Sexual Misconduct Allegations
full_text: Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All November 3, 2026 7:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Media set up outside London's High Court on Oct. 8, 2026 Courtesy of Getty Logo text A judge has ruled that an unnamed British celebrity facing allegations of “inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women” can be named in the press, but will remain anonymous while an appeal is lodged. The man had sought an injunction to prevent two news organisations, ITN and Guardian News and Media, from publishing his identity, over fears that he would be “highly likely” to kill himself. He maintained that the suicide risk is not attributed to any wrongdoing but because of what his lawyers described as “trial by media.” Related Stories Business Tokyo: Industry Insiders Skeptical of Bold Japanese Government Plans for Overseas Content Sales Push Business Tokyo: Japan's New Production Incentives Risk Doing as Much Harm as Good In a judgment that came Tuesday, Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction request and said: “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.” According to BBC News , London’s High Court heard that the celebrity denies that he abused “his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them.” Lawyers for ITN and the Guardian said his suicide risk could be mitigated and that there was no basis “to restrain the publication of public interest journalism.” Justice Nicklin had previously said there was “significant public interest” in the proceedings and that “this is a difficult and important case… The court must determine it fairly, on the evidence and legal submissions.” The British press have been warned against publishing any details that could identify the celebrity. Sara Mansoori, the lawyer representing the celebrity, told the judge in written submissions: “This is not a case where an individual has spuriously raised ‘mental health’ concerns in the face of an impending publication that they do not wish to occur… The claimant has attempted suicide twice as a result of these matters, been hospitalised for months, been the subject of involuntary detention and been examined by multiple — now more than 10 — doctors.” Mansoori also said the man “has no intention of returning to public life.” THR

title: Sony Partners With Lionsgate on Destin Daniel Cretton’s ‘Naruto’ Movie (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All November 3, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Naruto' Courtesy of Crunchyroll Logo text Lionsgate has partnered with Sony Pictures for its high-profile feature adaptation of Naruto . The deal, which came after competitive, multi-studio bidding, will see Sony co-finance the movie and take on international distribution of the live-action feature film that is based on the manga by Masashi Kishimoto that grew into a global entertainment brand. Lionsgate has now officially greenlit the project, which is the follow-up feature for Destin Daniel Cretton , who his coming off the $2.5 billion success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Cretton is writing the script and will direct and produce. Production slated to begin in spring 2027, with Lionsgate continuing to oversee the film’s development and production and handle domestic distribution. Related Stories Business Lionsgate Inks Deal With Meta to Bring New 'Hunger Games' Movie to VR Glasses Movies 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' First Reactions That Sony’s motion picture group, headed by Tom Rothman, would come out on top seems almost pre-ordained. Cretton in September signed a three-year first-look producing deal with the studio, signaling a strong relationship with his Brand New Day partner. And Sony, which is headquartered in Japan, is also the home of Crunchyroll, the popular and arguably largest streaming service that focuses on anime. “With their deep expertise in manga and anime and global distribution prowess, Sony Pictures is a perfect partner for Naruto , and we’re thrilled to join forces with Tom Rothman and his team to bring this extraordinary property to audiences around the world,” said Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson in a statement. “We share an enormous ambition for Naruto and a commitment to making this a truly global cinematic event that stays true to what millions of existing fans love and invites so many more to embrace what makes it truly special. Fogelson added, “I’m tremendously proud of Erin Westerman and James Myers for their work developing this film and bringing Destin aboard, and of Helen Lee-Kim for securing Sony as our international partner. Ari Arad, Tetsu Fujimura, and our producing team also deserve huge thanks for their hard work and support.” Stated Rothman, Sony’s Motion Picture Group CEO and chairman, “Lionsgate has done a masterful job in putting together an A-level adaptation, and we are honored to be chosen as their partner. Not to mention, we had a sweet success this summer with Destin and are delighted to be back in his capable hands.” Naruto is the coming-of-age story of a young and enthusiastic ninja named Naruto Uzumaki who wants to grow up to be the leader of his ninja village but also happens to have the spirit of a nine-tailed demon fox inside him. The story was serialized in Japan’s popular Weekly Shonen Jump from 1999 to 2014 and later spawned a couple of popular animated series that ran for years on Cartoon Network and Disney XD. Naruto sits in a rarefied tier of entertainment properties that have achieved an extraordinary global reach, enduring popularity, and cultural impact. Kishimoto’s manga has sold more than 250 million copies across over 60 countries and territories, growing into a multibillion-dollar franchise. The anime adaptation has reached audiences in more than 145 countries and territories. “As a longtime fan of Naruto , I’ve always loved that beneath the extraordinary action is a story filled with heart, humor, and humanity. Kishimoto-sensei created a world where unlikely heroes do extraordinary things, and that’s what makes it so special,” said Cretton in a statement. “Lionsgate has been an incredible partner, and I’m thrilled to reunite with the fantastic team at Sony. Together, we’re committed to capturing everything fans love about Naruto while introducing it to a whole new generation.” Avi Arad, Ari Arad and Emmy Yu are producing for Arad Productions. Cretton is producing alongside Jeyun Munford through his company, Hisako. Charles Melton is the only actor on board to star and is said to be playing Kakashi Hatake, the elite ninja mentor figure to the main character and his friends. The search for the actor to inhabit Naruto is currently underway. Erin Westerman and James Myers are overseeing the project for Lionsgate. THR

The film, directed by Luc Walpoth (“In Tandem,” “Dead Money”), is set to begin production in April 2027. WestEnd will launch sales at the upcoming American Film Market. Related Stories Box Office: 'You Can See Everything' Beats 'Clayface' for No. 1 With $11.4 Million in Sleepy Halloween Weekend 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win Set in a sun-soaked coastal paradise, “Breakwater” follows two women desperate for a way out. Iris (Kurylenko) is trapped in a toxic marriage, while Daya is a bartender desperate to escape her dead-end hometown. A chance encounter brings them together, and they hatch a plan to blackmail Iris’ sadistic husband Avery (Pettyfer) aboard his luxury yacht. But what seems like the perfect escape quickly spirals out of control. Stranded on the high seas, with nowhere to run and no one to trust, Iris and Daya find their carefully laid plan turning into a fight for survival. The film is produced by Kurt Wimmer (“The Beekeeper 1 & 2,” “Law Abiding Citizen,” “Point Break”), Jib Polhemus (“The Mechanic,” “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider,” “The Expendables 2”), Hannah Leader (“Mary,” “Freud’s Last Session,” “A Visit to Grandpa’s”) and Tad Daggerhart (“Black Lotus,” “Coyotes”), who also penned the script (“Expend4bles,” “Black Lotus”). James Ireland (“Echo Boomers”) executive produces for Dark Dreams Entertainment. “Breakwater” reunites WestEnd with Polhemus following their collaborations on action thriller “Scorpion,” also starring Pettyfer, alongside Clive Owen (currently in post-production), and “Zealot,” starring Kodi Smit-McPhee and Djimon Hounsou. Production in Malta will be overseen by Malta Film Service, led by partners Jean Pierre Magro and Vadim Fortunin. With credits including “Not Without Hope,” “Hounds of War” and “Blood on the Crown,” the company will manage on-the-ground line production, local crew integration, and rebate structuring across the shoot. Walpoth said: “’Breakwater’ is a Mediterranean neo-noir thriller about lust, greed, betrayal and the desire to escape. Set against a gorgeous coastal backdrop, the film contrasts sun-drenched beauty with the darker tensions beneath the surface. Visually, I want to create a world that feels both sensual and unsettling, building from simmering suspense into a propulsive, high-stakes thriller as plans unravel and loyalties shift on the open sea.” Maya Amsellem, managing director of WestEnd, said: “’Breakwater’ is a gripping thriller with a fantastic cast in Olga and Alex and a hugely experienced creative team behind it. Luc has a distinctive cinematic vision for the film, blending the atmosphere of classic noir with the pace and intensity of a contemporary thriller. We’re delighted to be teaming up again with Jib Polhemus on such an exciting project, and look forward to introducing the film to buyers at AFM .” WestEnd’s wider AFM slate includes new supernatural horror “Sketchbook,” starring Woody Norman and Billie Piper (shooting early 2027); Tim Blake Nelson’s “The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd,” starring Amanda Seyfried and Scoot McNairy (screening at AFM); “A Visit to Grandpa’s,” starring Academy Award winners Anthony Hopkins and Catherine Zeta-Jones (in post-production); “Margot & Rudi,” a romantic drama directed by Anthony Fabian, starring Naomi Watts (in pre-production); action-thriller “Scorpion,” starring Pettyfer and Owen (in post-production); high-concept thriller “Ignition,” starring Maisie Williams; and “Unspeakable,” a horror from Corinna Faith, starring Eliza Scanlen and Essie Davis (in post-production). title: British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars View All November 3, 2026 6:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images A well-known British man has lost his bid for an injunction against ITN and The Guardian to prevent the media outlets from publishing allegations of sexual misconduct. In a High Court judgment, the star’s claim for an injunction was denied, but a temporary order preventing the man (known as PPT in court proceedings) from being named remains in place pending an appeal. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Oscars: Every Best Picture Winner Back To The Beginning In 1929 The case has generated significant interest in the UK, sparking widespread social media speculation about the identity of the man at the heart of the allegations. “The claimant’s claim for an injunction was dismissed,” said Mr Justice Nicklin in a judgment Tuesday, per BBC and Sky News. Watch on Deadline “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.” During a hearing, PPT’s legal team argued that publishing would be “highly likely” to lead to his death by suicide after he had made two previous attempts to take his own life. Gavin Millar, who made the case for ITN and The Guardian , argued that the news organizations had a duty to publish information that was in the public interest. The two outlets are seeking to publish allegations of inappropriate and exploitative sexual activities with girls and young women based on the accounts of more than 30 sources, The Guardian reported. In a written submission to the court, PPT’s lawyers said: “It is important to understand that this drastic effect on the claimant is not from guilt of the wrongdoing alleged (which is denied) but because of shame arising from deep-rooted childhood trauma and the fear of ‘trial by media.'” The court heard that PPT had made two previous attempts to kill himself: In May, when ITN and The Guardian gave him an opportunity to respond to the allegations; and in July, when he absconded from a secure hospital. ITN is the British news group behind ITV News, Channel 4 News, and Skydance’s 5 News.
