title: Mark Lazarus: MS NOW Not Experiencing the Viewer “Fatigue” Lachlan Murdoch Complained About
full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All November 3, 2026 6:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source MS NOW's new Times Square studio MS NOW MS NOW doesn’t have that viewer “fatigue” problem Lachlan Murdoch was going on about. Versant CEO Mark Lazarus was teed up with the word in a question asked Tuesday by a member of the analyst community. The analyst himself was teed up by a phrase Murdoch, the Fox CEO, used on his own company’s quarterly earnings conference call . “Yesterday, Fox called out some viewership fatigue on news leading up to the midterms,” Morgan Stanley’s Sean Diffley said during the Q&A portion of this morning’s Versant third quarter earnings call. “I’m curious how you would describe what you’re seeing most recently on MS NOW.” “We’re not seeing currently not seeing any fatigue with our audiences,” Lazarus responded. “Our audiences are active and vibrant and growing for MS NOW, and for that matter, with CNBC. I think it’s a testament to the quality of our product, to the voices that we have on there, and to the trust that our viewers have in our brands and in our talent. But we’re showing growth, and we have for…many months in a row on MS NOW, and that’s encouraging.” It was a fair shot to take following the TV ratings excuse Murdoch introduced just 24 hours earlier. “What we are seeing is some viewer fatigue, where our viewers have gone through an incredible news cycle last year with the inauguration, the Charlie Kirk tragedy, DOGE, flooding, it was an incredible news cycle last year,” Murdoch said, comparing what is currently happening to the 2006 midterms, when President George W. Bush was midway through his second term. “Those viewers are not switching to another news channel, they are just fatigued and watching slightly less television overall. We have seen this playbook, and we know how to move through it.” Murdoch has his own fair shot chambered for Laz: Fox News Channel is still beating CNN and MS NOW combined in viewers. Murdoch quipped on his call that Fox News really shouldn’t really consider CNN and MS NOW its “peers” given the ratings chasm between first and second place in cable news. At times, FNC’s Nielsen numbers rival those of the major broadcast news brands, Murdoch pointed out. Today is Election Day — get out there and vote. THR

title: Johnny Depp on His One Condition to Return as Jack Sparrow for ‘Pirates of the Caribbean 6’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All November 3, 2026 6:18am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Johnny Depp and Orlando Bloom in 'Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl.' Walt Disney/Courtesy Everett Collection Johnny Depp is open to reprising his role as Captain Jack Sparrow should Pirates of the Caribbean return but for one reason. In an interview with Entertainment Tonight , the actor explained what would be his motivating factor to don the pirate hat again. “If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they are going to top off the Pirates franchise… the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note,” the actor said. Related Stories TV A Royal Surprise: 'The Remarried Empress' Releases One Day Early on Disney+ and Hulu TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Disney Night Makes Magic (3 Perfect Scores!) as Group Dances Return, Another Celeb Departs: See the Scores, Who Went Home He continued, “I will go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything. Doesn’t matter… if it’s Jerry, I trust him. We have a deep friendship.” Depp headlined the five Pirates of the Caribbean films that released from 2003 to 2017. Bruckheimer, who produced all five previous films, previously told The Hollywood Reporter in 2022 that they were “getting very close” with Pirates 6 and even had a “very good script.” The producer also noted that Pirates would be rebooted “so that is easier to put together“ given “you don’t have to wait for certain actors.” The last Pirates of the Caribbean movie, Dead Men Tell No Tales , was released was in 2017 and starred Depp, Javier Bardem and Kaya Scodelario, as well as returning franchise cast members Geoffrey Rush , Orlando Bloom , and Keira Knightley . Bruckheimer has been candid about work on a new Pirates film which would have Jeff Nathanson writing the script. Another reported film, penned by Christina Hodson from Birds of Prey , was to star Margot Robbie . In her Vanity Fair 2022 cover story Robbie said of the film, “We had an idea and we were developing it for a while, ages ago, to have more of a female-led — not totally female-led, but just a different kind of story — which we thought would’ve been really cool, but I guess they don’t want to do it.” However, Bruckheimer has said he still intended on getting a reboot and Robbie‘s film made: “We hope to get ’em both made, and I think Disney agrees they really want to make the Margot one, too,” Bruckheimer told Entertainment Weekly. “I think he’s cracked it,” Bruckheimer also told EW of Nathanson’s script. “He’s got an amazing third act. We just gotta clean up the first and second and then we’ll get there. But he wrote a great, great third act.” Bruckheimer previously told EW that he would welcome Depp to return to the role and had conversations with the actor about it. “It’s a reboot, but if it was up to me, he would be in it,” Bruckheimer said. “I love him. He’s a good friend. He’s an amazing artist, and he’s a unique look. He created Captain Jack. That was not on the page; that was him doing a little Pepé Le Pew and Keith Richards. That was his interpretation of Jack Sparrow.” THR

title: Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With Divisions Eyeing Up To 20% In Cost Savings
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro , Nellie Andreeva November 2, 2026 7:29pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Walt Disney Studios Exterior Gilbert Flores/Getty Images The Walt Disney company is laying the groundwork for more cuts, with thousands poised to be impacted. According to sources, the new round of layoffs will be made across multiple divisions, including TV networks and the motion picture studio, at varying amounts. As is customary in the run-up to staff reductions, managers of the affected teams have been given targets, with some asked to achieve as much as 20% in annual cost savings, we hear. Disney declined to comment on the latest cuts, first reported by Bloomberg, whose exact timing is unclear. Related Stories Executives Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Exec Hans Ku Chief Product Officer News 'Star Wars' Voices & Sounds Made Available To Gamers And Creators By Tech Firm Voicemod There have been ongoing layoffs at Disney throughout the year following Josh D’Amaro taking over as CEO from Bob Iger on March 18. In April, 1,000 roles would be eliminated, followed by several hundred in July, with Pixar and National Geographic among the divisions most affected . Watch on Deadline The process accelerated in August when the entertainment conglomerate extended a Voluntary Early Retirement Offer to longtime executives. That process has now been completed, with some sources indicating that more eligible managers opted for the package than anticipated. The VERO was always considered a precursor to layoffs. “This is one of several actions we’re taking to reshape our organization, including involuntary staff reductions that have already begun in some areas and will continue into next year,” Disney EVP and Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman wrote at in memo back in August. Since then, a couple of hundred employees were laid off in late September , largely in areas such as tech and HR, and last week, another 100-200 employees in its Experiences division were pink slipped, the majority of them at Disney’s Imagineering campus in Glendale. “I think like all of our similarly situated competitors, and certainly all of our competitors in the tech industry, there is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Dana Walden, President and Chief Creative Officer of The Walt Disney Company , said about the continuous layoffs during Bloomberg’s Screentime conference last month. “Technology set their sights on our business, and we must survive and thrive and grow. That’s what we’re going to do.” D’Amaro has put a focus on cost reductions since ascending to the top Disney job earlier this year. At the most recent Disney earnings call, he spoke about using some of the savings to invest in growth areas. “When our teams work smarter, we can serve more people across our parks and digital platforms and do it more cost-effectively,” he said. “That frees up capital to reinvest aggressively in what drives long-term value: new content and next generation guest experiences, as well as technology infrastructure that keeps Disney at the forefront of entertainment.” Disney’s global head count stood just north of 230,000 as of the end of the most recent fiscal year. title: New Anti-Harassment Laws Lead To Questions From UK Film & TV Industry
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max John Leeson Dies: Actor Who Voiced Iconic Role In ‘Doctor Who’ Was 83 Ex-YMU Global Entertainment Boss Launches London Agency Repping Creators Including Topjaw’s Jesse Burgess Russell Brand’s Defense Argues Channel 4 Film “Poisoned Well Of Justice Deliberately” View All November 3, 2026 1:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty EXCLUSIVE: Big UK production groups and studios have been busily preparing for new anti-harassment laws that will impact the film and TV industry, but questions remain. Last Friday, UK-wide legislation came into force that means employers are now liable for harassment of their staff, cast and crew by third parties. Employers must take “all reasonable steps” to prevent harassment, the law now states, and claims can be made up to six months after an incident takes place. The legislation is part of the UK’s much-discussed Employment Rights Act, one of the ruling Labour Paty’s flagship pieces of reform. Related Stories News International Insider: European TV In Peril; Venice & TIFF Latest; Mercedes Ron Interview News International Revenues Of $2.1B Boost British TV Makers, Census Finds, As Pact Warns BBC Must Avoid "Managed Decline" The adustment has led many big production houses and studios to update their harassment policies in preparation, we are told. “These changes give victims much stronger legal protections,” said the government when the legislation, which applies to all industries, came into force. Watch on Deadline In practice, this change means that if cast or crew are harassed during a production by a third party, be that an agent, someone on location or even someone who has nothing to do with the project, the production company or studio could now be liable for the claim. “This is a significant change,” said Elizabeth Peyton-Jones, who runs The Talent Trust, which takes real-time reaction data from crew working on productions. “As an employer, you can’t now say, ‘I can’t control what other people do.’ You have to take responsibility. And the duty of care reaches beyond the set.” Producers we spoke with were mostly aware that the legislation was coming in and have been preparing, but they still have questions over just how far this duty of care reaches. Peyton-Jones used the example of a wrap party, where people who didn’t work on a project could be invited and incidents could happen. Would the producer then be liable for the actions of that third party? “Wrap parties are an interesting example because they are informal,” she added. “People have been working together for a long time; stress and exhaustion are high. If someone doesn’t speak up until long after production has wrapped, and if nothing was time-stamped and no action was taken, then a production company can’t simply say it didn’t know. It should therefore have a mechanism for people to raise concerns.” Deadline understands at least one large production outfit considers wrap parties, late-night working and staying in hotels as part of its risk assessments. “Where does the buck stop?” Other examples floated to Deadline that require clarity include incidents that take place on the street when crew are doing vox pops, harassment on transport on the way to-and-from a set, or situations where crew have to accompany third parties for filming. The vision behind the legislation, communicated by the government last week, is that “whether a passenger harassing a bus driver, a waiter being intimidated by diners, or a shop worker dealing with abuse from customers, reforms will ensure that unacceptable behaviour is not treated as part of the job.” Max Rumney, the deputy CEO of producer trade body Pact , which represents hundreds of UK indies, said the question of “where does the buck stop?” is confusing his members, and he doesn’t feel he has all the answers from government. “In many ways this is a law for environments that are slightly different to ours,” he explained. Pact’s legal chief sent a note to all members last week, which Deadline has seen, urging them to “update their anti-harassment and bullying policies, if you have not already done so, to ensure that you remain compliant with the law.” We are also told that training body ScreenSkills has updated the anti-bullying and harassment module on its training passport in line with the legislation. This all feels necessary. Just a few weeks ago, a survey from UK arbitration service Acas found that two-fifths of employers across all industries were unaware of these changes in law. Making things more confusing is the fact that the law has technically come into force but detailed guidance will only be available from early 2027. Deadline understands the UK’s Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, and Digital, Culture, Media and Sport have both been prepping the industry, meeting with trade associations, hosting webinars and pushing employers to update their policies. The departments wouldn’t be drawn on specific examples of when an employer would be liable for harassment or not. We spoke with big production groups in the UK who said they have been preparing for the change but wouldn’t come on the record to discuss further. One HR executive at a big player said they had updated contractual terms for future productions in order to account for the new third-parties law. Of course, some indies are much smaller, often one-or-two-person bands, and many don’t have HR departments, which could lead to issues with the new law. Movies are often run by production outfits only created for that particular project before being shut down. If an incident takes place on one such movie but is only reported months afterwards, the responsibility could fall on a company that has just been dissolved. Pact’s Rumney, however, reckons bigger productions will be more problematic. “Small indies make smaller productions and they know how to do these things,” he added. In the UK film and TV industry, harassment remains a huge topic, in part due to high-profile instances of allegations in recent years. The anti-harassment legislation came into force on the day a prosecuting barrister delivered closing arguments at the Russell Brand trial, for which the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. Brand denies all allegations and says all relationships were consensual. Those we have spoken with rejected the idea that the new law will lead to a flood of harassment complaints, with many barriers that prevent the industry’s majority freelance workforce from making claims still in place. “I think there will still be resistance [to complaining],” said Peyton-Jones. Talent Trust research has previously pointed to a “silence gap” on UK productions. A report recently found 40% did not feel respected or treated with dignity on a production and yet more than three quarters (76%) didn’t feel they could speak up without worrying about unfair repercussions. Many concerned industry folk are hopeful the “silence gap” will begin to close now that the long-expected CIISA anonymous whistleblowing service has launched . The new harassment laws could contribute to a further closing of the gap, but this feels a bit of a way off. title: ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars

On Alan Carr’s Life’s A Beach Podcast , the Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire star was incredulous about a report in The Mail on Sunday claiming he told Celebrity Traitors producers that he was uncomfortable with “macho banter” during filming. “I’ve never had stuff made up about me before,” Acaster told Carr, who won the first season of The Celebrity Traitors on the BBC. “There was something in the papers that said I’d complained cos Rob and Romesh had been teasing me.” Related Stories News 'The Celebrity Traitors' Finale Draws Record Audience To BBC News 'The Celebrity Traitors': BBC Says It's "Categorically Untrue" James Acaster Made Complaint About Co-Stars' "Macho Banter" “I was like: I’ve been friends with those guys for like over 10 years. They were lovely the entire show. I didn’t complain about any of my fellow players. It was so completely fabricated. They contacted my agents and Rob and Romesh’s agents [and] all of them said: ‘That is categorically untrue.’ They [the Mail ] went: ‘Cool, printing it tomorrow.'” Watch on Deadline In a story splashed on the front page of the Mail on Sunday last month, the newspaper quoted a “snitch” on the show as saying: “Rob and Romesh clearly thought they were having a bit of a laugh, but James began to feel quite a lot of it was at his expense, and away from the cameras he started to get annoyed and upset by it. title: ‘Queen Silvia’ Team Hopes For Multiple Seasons After Royal Drama’s Cannes Premiere
full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart More International Deals For ‘Sherlock & Daughter’ Ahead Of UK & Ireland Premiere On HBO Max ‘Queen Silvia’ Team Hopes For Multiple Seasons After Royal Drama’s Cannes Premiere Terry Sanders Wraps Documentary ‘On Rescuing Democracy And The Rule Of Law’ View All November 3, 2026 1:21am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Queen Silvia' Becker Films, Amazon, Joyn, Pyjama Pictures Queen Silvia was crowned in Cannes with a world premiere screening for the upcoming royal drama series. German actress Alicia von Rittberg ( Call My Agent Berlin ), who stars as the titular Silvia Sommerlath, and Swedish actor Edvin Endre ( Vikings ), who plays Crown Prince Carl Gustaf, were in town for the premiere. A grand piano was in situ in the auditorium for a live performance of Dancing Queen, the megahit that ABBA performed at a pre-wedding gala for the royal couple. The royal romance is destined for Prime Video in German-speaking territories and the Nordics and SAT.1 in Germany. Beta Film is selling it internationally. SVT has taken a second window in Sweden. Related Stories News 'Carrie's Mike Flanagan Reflects On Supernatural YA Drama & Says 'Warhammer 40,000' Series Has "Very Cool And Unexpected On-Ramp" News Amazon Shares Fall On Q3 Earnings Miss As Big Tech Market Rout Continues “Royal love stories are working tremendously well,” Justus Riesenkampff, EVP Nordics & Benelux at Beta Film, told Deadline. “We’ve had a lot of classic period pieces, but people are intrigued in these modern royal stories. Queen Silvia has a lot of elements that will also resonate with the younger audiences. It is an ideal setup and also has the potential for future seasons.” Watch on Deadline Silvia met Carl Gustaf, the Crown Prince of Sweden, when he was a guest at the ill-fated 1972 Munich Olympic Games, where Silvia was working. Season 1 focuses on the early years of their relationship, from the day they met until the eve of their marriage. “At first glance, it’s a classical royal story; a noble person marries a commoner,” said Carsten Kelber, Producer at German label Pyjama Pictures, which produces with Sweden’s Unlimited Stories. “But in this story it is very different and there are a lot of surprises that lie within the main characters and their backgrounds,” He added” “A lot of the usual tropes or patterns are turned upside down in this story. The genre is clear, it’s a romantic drama, but it’s also a very modern view on relationships and female empowerment.” The royal couple remain married and a regal drama that includes many characters still alive has echoes of The Crown as well as Dutch series Máxima , which Beta also distributes. The Queen Silvia producers notified the royal family the series was happening. Miguel Alexandre ( Gran Paradiso ) directs from a screenplay he penned with Lisa Hofer ( Black Island ) and Pauline Wolff ( VAKA ). As with shows that have gone before such as The Crown , the series covers real-life historic milestones, but the conversations and drama that took place behind closed doors is where the writers’ skills come into play. Kelber said: “What happened in the car on the way to the event? What did they talk about, what was his or her take on what was happening? This is the fun thing to think about. It is, of course, fictional freedom. Our director likes to call it ‘poetic truth.’” The setup lends itself very naturally to a big European drama involving producers from Sweden and Germany. “The story takes place both in Germany and Sweden and they move back and forth and there are both Swedish and German characters in it; it’s very seamlessly a [Swedish-German] coproduction,” said Frida Wallman from Unlimited Stories. title: appointment of Casey Bloys
full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White , Jill Goldsmith October 5, 2026 6:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Clockwise Top L-R: Casey Bloys, George Cheeks, Dana Goldberg, Josh Greenstein, James Gunn, Peter Safran, JB Perette, Mark Thompson, Bari Weiss Skydance After a year of negotiations, false starts, and internal and external politicking, the question of who will run the combined media and entertainment giant created by Paramount acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery has been answered. As anticipated, the company, which will be called simply Skydance , has set top roles for Casey Bloys , as co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance DTC, and George Cheeks as head of Skydance TV. JB Perrette is making the jump from WBD as Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC. Related Stories Culture List Of Hollywood & Media Layoffs From Paramount To Warner Bros Discovery To CNN & More Executives Skydance Chief Communications Officer Melissa Zukerman Unveils Leadership Team, Executive Departures Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will co-chair the motion picture group. James Gunn and Peter Safran will remain atop DC Studios. As reported, Warner Bros Motion Picture Chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy‘s last day will be Tuesday , when the merger is set to officially close. Watch on Deadline Mark Thompson was named Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of CNN Worldwide , Bari Weiss editor-in-chief of CBS News. See list below. All will be reporting directly to co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. CEO Corporate Leadership Team Andy Gordon, President Dennis Cinelli, Chief Financial Officer Makan Delrahim, Chief Legal Officer and President, Global Corporate Affairs Dane Glasgow, Chief Product Officer Rebecca Mall, Chief Marketing Officer Melissa Zukerman, Chief Communications Officer CEO Business Leadership Team Casey Bloys, Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DTC George Cheeks, Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance TV Dana Goldberg, Co-Chair, Skydance Motion Picture Group Josh Greenstein, Co-Chair, Skydance Motion Picture Group James Gunn, Co-Chairman of DC Studios JB Perrette, Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC Peter Safran, Co-Chairman of DC Studios CEO News Executive Leadership Team Mark Thompson , Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of CNN Worldwide Bari Weiss, Editor-in-Chief of CBS News A complete list of the merged company’s executive leadership team will be issued soon after close. “I’m incredibly proud to introduce the team that will lead Skydance forward, a group that reflects the ambition behind this historic combination,” Ellison said. “Together, Paramount and Warner Bros. will form a creative-first home with the scale, imagination and technology to define entertainment for a generation. The leaders joining me have built some of the most beloved franchises and businesses in the industry, and they share a deep respect for the creative process and a belief that great stories have the power to entertain, unite and inspire audiences around the world. Their talent, experience and ambition are exactly what this moment demands, and together we will build a next-generation global media company that leads the industry in creative excellence and innovation, and delivers for audiences, creators, partners and shareholders alike.” Today’s lineup comes just over a year after news broke that Paramount was exploring a deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery , a month after David Ellison’s Skydance closed its $8.4 billion deal to buy Paramount . Ellison founded Skydance in 2010, backed by his father Larry Ellison, the billionaire co-founder of Oracle. He expanded the company over the years, adding sports and animation divisions to film and television production. He launched his recent ambitious sequence of acquisitions by first acquiring Shari Redstone’s majority ownership stake in Paramount in August of 2025 and turning almost immediately to pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery, ultimately prying it from the arms of Netflix with a series of sweetened offers. The WBD deal, a smaller company buying a much larger one, is one of the biggest leveraged buyouts in history and will load the combined entity with about $80 billion in debt and hefty interest expenses to service it, creating fears of layoffs. Ellison has promised Wall Street $6 billion in cost savings but has insisted most of that will not come from jobs cuts . News of who will run the new Skydance, which brings together brands such as Harry Potter, Mission Impossible , Friends and Yellowstone , had started to emerge over the last week. The org chart began to shape after a court settlement cleared the decks for Paramount-WBD to come together in the massive deal valued at $110 billion. On September 30, former Mattel CEO Kreiz, who was also previously CEO of Endemol, was named Co-CEO of the company alongside Ellison. “Our goals as a team are to establish Skydance as the premier Hollywood content engine and home for the world’s leading storytellers, accelerate our integrated DTC platform with the best content, leading-edge technology and superior consumer experience, and optimize our highly profitable linear TV portfolio, reaching audiences globally across every entertainment vertical,” Kreiz said today. “Together, we will: Win in storytelling by leveraging our creative capabilities, talent relationships, production prowess and expansive library of iconic IP; Build the most technologically capable media company through a modern tech platform to enhance the user experience, improve how we work and achieve operating efficiencies; and Lead in a crowded market by capitalizing on our scale, assets and global reach to compete in an evolving marketplace, drive synergies and grow our business.” Cindy Holland, who was Paramount’s Chair of Direct-to-Consumer, ostensibly running Paramount+, was the first to officially reveal she was stepping down ahead of the deal closing. Holland’s departure answered one of the biggest questions heading into the combination: who would lead streaming. That move telegraphed that Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and HBO Max Content, was in line for this major new role at the new company, as indicated in Holland’s departure note to colleagues on Sept. 29. “David is optimizing for HBO stability,” she wrote. In it’s note today, the company said the new team is “designed to drive transformation and growth, deepen collaboration across the business, and ensure the combined company is positioned to execute on its mission.” Ellison intends to focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation. Kreiz will focus on tday-to-day management and integrating of the combined business. Andy Gordon will work closely with both on strategic priorities across its businesses. All three will serve on the board of directors, with Ellison as chairman. title: Bosses At ‘Clangold’ Producer Beetz Brothers Hail Skydance For Backing Casey Bloys: “A Strong Sign The HBO Line Will Continue”
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Titan1Studios Adapting Stephen R. Bown’s ‘The Company: The Rise and Fall Of The Hudson’s Bay Empire’ As Historical Drama Series Bosses At ‘Clangold’ Producer Beetz Brothers Hail Skydance For Backing Casey Bloys: “A Strong Sign The HBO Line Will Continue” ‘Carrie’s Mike Flanagan Reflects On Supernatural YA Drama & Says ‘Warhammer 40,000’ Series Has “Very Cool And Unexpected On-Ramp” View All November 3, 2026 2:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Clangold' HBO Max/Eveliene Klink Ever since Paramount and Warner Bros. merged, producers around the world have been wondering what it will mean for their prospects. For Germany ‘s Beetz Brothers , which launches crime doc Clangold on HBO Max globally on November 13, the appointment of Casey Bloys as Skydance’s content chief is a “strong sign” those making high-end, mainstream productions will be well served. Georg Tschurtschenthaler, Chief Creative Officer at the Berlin-based Beetz, addressed the merger in an interview with Deadline, noting that “some information” about the new business was trickling down to international producers. Related Stories News 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 Star Taissa Farmiga Talks Gladys' "Intense" First Episode Executives Skydance TV & DTC Co-Chair JB Perrette Unveils Leadership Team, Executive Departures “There was relief because Casey Bloys remains at the top of the structure, which is a strong sign that the HBO line will continue,” he said. “The launch of [HBO Max drama] Four Blocks Zero was a big thing in Germany. All the newspapers reported on it, and internationally it reached the HBO top 10. That was a very good push. The signs seem positive, although that is simply what we know at this stage.” Watch on Deadline Christian Beetz, co-CEO and co-founder at Beetz, added discussions for program orders remain separate with HBO Max and Paramount+, though Skydance co-CEO David Ellison has said they will eventually merge into one service. “They currently have very different programs,” he said. “I think there is still some time to go.” HBO Max’s upcoming four-part doc Clangold centers on one of the biggest criminal cases in Germany’s history, when a 100kg Canadian gold coin known as ‘Big Maple Leaf’ was stolen from Berlin’s Bode Museum in 2017. The story, directed by Jan Zabeil, follows the investigation into the audacious heist, the legal proceedings and prosecutor Katrin Faust’s cat-and-mouse struggle with perpetrators, but is considered humorous and light-hearted at times as the absurdity of the situation is revealed. Members of the Remmo family, an influential Mhallami-Arab group in Berlin whose image is fueled by rap and film, were ultimately convicted of the robbery and the doc looks closely at them. Beetz restructure For the Leonine Studios-owned Beetz, which is known for docs such as Sundance doc Eternal You , the launch of Clangold comes after it restructured this year under six genre labels. Christian Beetz and Georg Tschurtschenthaler Beetz Brothers Premium content arm Beetz Originals was responsible for Clangold . The others are Elon Musk Unveiled – The Tesla Experiment producer Beetz Investigate; Wacken – Hearts Full of Metal maker Beetz Music; Beetz Sports, which is making a film about World Cup winner turned extreme sports competitor André Schürrle; The First Lady maker Beetz Queer; and Beetz Factual, which made Trump’s America . Tschurtschenthaler and Beetz said this was partly in response to a belief the market is becoming increasingly commercial just as the film festivals that have traditionally underpinned their business model chase artistic movies. “We had an internal debate about how to position ourselves, and we arrived at the phrase, ‘We want to entertain — entertainment that resonates,'” said Beetz, who launched the company with his brother Reinhardt 26 years ago. “In contrast to some other projects, we add complexity and depth because we think there is a big audience that wants to be entertained but also wants to learn something,” added Tschurtschenthaler. “That was the core of Clangold . It is a heist story, so but have reinvented the crime genre a little – it is very funny and the first episode is really entertaining, but a second layer goes deeper into the controversial topics of organized crime, migration and integration.” He added the restructure was also based on expertize within the company. “In this more challenging market you need to be outstanding with every project,” he said, while Beetz added the global streamers’ focus on entertainment meant, “Every click counts and that is where the money is.” Beetz estimated his company has won in excess of 150 awards, but has shifted focus away from the likes of IDFA and Sundance to the International Emmys and other ceremonies that are “closer to the market” in 2026. “This is a substantial change,” added Tschurtschenthaler “In the old days – maybe three to five years ago – having a film in competition at Sundance would automatically trigger sales and bring in a large audience. That is not the case anymore. The digital world works differently, and that has led to a fairly drastic change in our strategy.” 2027 plans Upcoming projects include ZDF doc Countdown to the Midterms , which follows how the race for Congress is shaping up on both sides, with analysis from the likes of Tucker Carlson, Phil Murphy and Karen Attiah. German filmmaker Marcel Mettelsiefen is directing the Beetz Factual show. Vienna , meanwhile, is a Beetz Original that goes inside the story of Taylor Swift’s three canceled concerts in the Austrian capital in August 2024 after intelligence was received about a planned terror attack by a teenager who was radicalized through TikTok. “We have the USP of Taylor Swift and the breaking-news element, but we are telling the inside story and exploring the relevance of a new type of Islamic terrorist — digital terrorists who do not necessarily speak Arabic or appear particularly religious,” said Tschurtschenthaler. “The story ultimately connects to the manosphere. At the end of the day, these are lost kids. Some move toward the right and some move in other directions.” The company’s Elon Musk doc, which looks into the alleged failure of the billionaire’s Tesla company to address concerns over deadly faults with the autopilot function of its self-driving cars, sold widely earlier this year . Kaleidoscope has the rights in the U.S., UK and Ireland, with Mediawan Rights selling it elsewhere. Mediawan, the French group that bought Beetz parent Leonine in 2024, has been looking at how its production assets can work together to fund projects. The company made news last month when it teamed with Reese Witherspoon to buy her Hello Sunshine business from Candle Media, adding it to a lineup also including Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment and Slow Horses producer See-Saw Films. Beetz chuckled at the idea of co-producing with Witherspoon, but said the bigger focus was identifying its own IP that could work internationally as scripted projects. “Then we can bring them together with the right people from the fiction side,” he added. Elsinore earned nominations for Best British Independent Film, Best Director for Simon Stone, Best Screenplay for Simon Beresford, Best Lead Performance for previous winner Andrew Scott, and Best Supporting Performance for Billie Piper. The film also received seven craft nominations, including Best Cinematography, Best Casting, Best Costume Design, Best Editing, Best Make-Up & Hair Design for Nadia Stacey, Best Original Music, and Best Production Design for Helen Scott. Watch on Deadline Ashley Walters’ debut feature Animol has seven nominations, including Best Debut Director Film for Walters and Breakthrough Producer for Tom Hawkins. The film’s acting leads, Tut Nyuot and Sekou Diaby, have two nominations each: Best Lead and Best Supporting Performance, alongside Breakthrough Performance Netflix. This year’s nominees for Best International Independent Film are Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden , Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love , Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo’s La Bola Negra , Jordan Firstman’s Club Kid , and Marine Atlan’s La Gradiva . title: France Opens War Crimes Investigation Into Beirut Deaths Of Artist-Filmmaker Ali Cherri’s Parents
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie France Opens War Crimes Investigation Into Beirut Deaths Of Artist-Filmmaker Ali Cherri’s Parents Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins, Danny Huston, Robert Aramayo & Chloe Pirrie Join Elle Fanning & Julianne Moore In Rebecca Miller’s ‘Moonsong: A Life In Seven Verses’ – AFM ‘Who Is Still Alive’ Trailer: Watermelon Pictures Sets U.S. Theatrical Release For Swiss Oscar Entry View All November 3, 2026 4:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Photo of a young Ali Cherri and his parents retrieved from the rubble of their bombed apartment building Ali Cherri The French War Crimes Unit has opened a judicial investigation into the Israeli army’s bombing of a residential building in Beirut in November 2024 in which seven civilians were killed, including the parents of Franco-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri . Related Stories News Neon Joins Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor’s Explosive Gaza-Israel Doc ‘NAZA’ News International Insider: Votes Cast In Israel & Brazil; Tokyo Drift; Domingo Corral Interview The decision comes six months after Cherri, who is known in the film world for his Cannes Directors’ Fortnight-selected feature The Dam, and the Paris-based International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) filed an official complaint to the unit about the incident. The case concerns the Israeli military’s bombing of a residential building in Beirut on November 26, 2024, just a few hours before a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah was due to come into effect. The strike destroyed three floors of the apartment block with Cherri’s father and mother, Mahmoud Naim Cherri and Nadira Hayek, as well as a domestic worker employed by the couple, Birki Negesa, among the seven civilians who were killed. Watch on Deadline Two investigating judges from the French War Crimes Unit have been appointed to investigate the case. “To our knowledge, this is the very first judicial investigation opened into the crimes committed by the Israeli army in Lebanon since October 2023,” said Clémence Bectarte, lawyer and coordinator of the FIDH Litigation Action Group. “We hope that this investigation will shed full light on the bombing of 26 November 2024, which we qualified as a war crime in our complaint.” Cherri, who divides his time between Paris and Beirut, is one of Lebanon’s best-known contemporary artists, whose work has shown at the Guggenheim, Tate Modern and the Jeu de Paume among many other galleries. As he holds dual French and Lebanese nationality, the judicial investigation will focus only on the bombing of his apartment. The French courts do not have jurisdiction over the events that led to the deaths of the victims, who were not French nationals. “The opening of this judicial investigation marks another important step in our fight against impunity and our struggle for justice for those who were killed. For my family and me, it is essential that this investigation establish responsibility and ensure that those who ordered and carried out this bombing are held accountable for their actions.” said Cherri. Tensions between Israel and militant group Hezbollah ratcheted up in 2023 when the latter intensified attacks along Israel’s northern border in the wake of the October 7 Hamas attacks on the south of the country. Israel launched a military campaign in Lebanon in September 2024, involving aerial bombardments and a ground invasion, which killed more than 4,000 people and displaced another one million inhabitants. The Israeli military has been accused of targeting buildings in Lebanon in a bid to take out Hezbollah militant operatives in full knowledge that civilians would also be caught in the strike. A fragile ceasefire has been in place since November 2024, with the Israeli army still occupying parts of southern Lebanon and sporadic skirmishes. title: Lucky Number Unveils First Image Of Hiam Abbass In Psychological Thriller ‘Daughter Of Eden’ – AFM
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Lucky Number Unveils First Image Of Hiam Abbass In Psychological Thriller ‘Daughter Of Eden’ – AFM France Opens War Crimes Investigation Into Beirut Deaths Of Artist-Filmmaker Ali Cherri’s Parents Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins, Danny Huston, Robert Aramayo & Chloe Pirrie Join Elle Fanning & Julianne Moore In Rebecca Miller’s ‘Moonsong: A Life In Seven Verses’ – AFM View All November 3, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daughter of Eden © Flower Market Films Ltd, Newgrange Pictures Limited, British Broadcasting Corporation, The British Film Institute 2026 EXCLUSIVE: Lucky Number has released a first image of Succession star Hiam Abbass in London-set psychological thriller Daughter of Eden , in which she plays a woman suspected of having connections with the Saddam Hussein regime in a past life. The Paris-based sales company is gearing up for an AFM sales launch for the debut feature of Iranian British director Ahmadi, after buzzy shorts including the BIFA nominated Bitter Sea and Leila’s Blues which screened at Cannes Directors’ Fortnight as part of Tunisia Factory. The cast also features Yasmin Al-Khudhairi ( ( A Good Girl’s Guide to Murder ), Amir El-Masry ( Giant ) and Lindsay Duncan ( Birdman ). Related Stories Casting Jeremy Renner & Josh Brolin Set For Orlando von Einsiedel's 'A Speck In The Sea'; 193 Launching Sales At AFM News Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins, Danny Huston, Robert Aramayo & Chloe Pirrie Join Elle Fanning & Julianne Moore In Rebecca Miller's 'Moonsong: A Life In Seven Verses' - AFM Al-Khudhairi stars as British Iraqi nurse who begins to suspect that one of her patients may be connected to the fate of her parents under Saddam Hussein’s rule in Iraq. Watch on Deadline Driven by a desperate need to uncover the truth about her family’s past, she becomes increasingly entangled in the life of her patient, as her search for answers threatens to consume her and blur the line between justice and revenge. Beyond its psychological thriller premise, Daughter of Eden explores the lasting trauma of political persecution and the legacy of violence across generations. “Daughter of Eden began with a question I kept coming back to: how far might someone go for justice when the past still feels painfully present? I wanted to explore the pain that can stay with a person long after the violence itself has ended,” said Ahmadi. The film is produced by Jack Tarling of Shudder Films ( Kneecap , God’s Own Country ) and Pietro Greppi of Lunapark Pictures ( Flux Gourmet ) in co-production with Jackie Larkin of Newgrange Pictures. It is funded by the BFI (awarding National Lottery funding) and BBC Film, in association with Screen Ireland, Civic Studios and Three Point Capital (TPC), with the BFI and BBC Film having previously developed the project. “We are very excited to be working on Fateme Ahmadi’s debut feature, a compelling psychological thriller that builds an unsettling sense of tension and uncertainty, drawing audiences deeper into its world until the very end,” said Lucky Number. “ Daughter of Eden skilfully revisits the perpetrator–victim relationship by taking a careful and in-depth look at the psychology of its characters, reflecting on the uncomfortable questions and exploring the lasting consequences of trauma and political violence.” Lucky Number will be screening a first promo-reel for the film at the AFM. “We’re excited to partner with Lucky Number to give an exclusive first glimpse of the film to distributors at AFM whilst we make the finishing touches,” said Tarling and Greppi. Lucky Number was launched by Olivier Barbier, Ola Byszuk and Lenny Porte in 2024 with a focus on ambitious French and international auteur films with a global appeal. Remaining true to its founding mission, its 2026 slate has featured Berlinale Perspectives title Where To? By Assaf Machnes; Cannes Un Certain Regard selection Strawberries by Laïla Marrakchi, which is Morocco’s 2027 Oscars entry; Directors’ Fortnight selected Death Has No Master by Jorge Thielen Armand, which is Venezuela’s entry, and Jacqueline Lentzou’s Venice Orizzonti Best Director winner Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra . title: More International Deals For ‘Sherlock & Daughter’ Ahead Of UK & Ireland Premiere On HBO Max
full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart More International Deals For ‘Sherlock & Daughter’ Ahead Of UK & Ireland Premiere On HBO Max ‘Queen Silvia’ Team Hopes For Multiple Seasons After Royal Drama’s Cannes Premiere Terry Sanders Wraps Documentary ‘On Rescuing Democracy And The Rule Of Law’ View All November 3, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sherlock & Daughter The CW, HBO Max EXCLUSIVE: Sherlock & Daughter is heading to a raft of new territories. The series is on The CW and HBO Max in the U.S. and is about to premiere on HBO Max in the UK and Ireland on November 5. From Starlings Entertainment in association with The CW, the series stars David Thewlis as iconic detective Sherlock Holmes and Blu Hunt as Amelia Rojas, a young Native American woman determined to prove to the world-famous sleuth that he is her father. Dougray Scott plays Holmes’ infamous nemesis Professor Moriarty. Public broadcasters RTP and CT have acquired it for Portugal and the Czech Republic respectively while other buyers include AB1 in France, Viasat in Poland and Magenta TV in Germany. In Belgium it has landed with SVOD service Streamz and Canal+ has acquired the show for pay TV in Austria and Switzerland. YES has taken it for Israel. Related Stories News Bosses At 'Clangold' Producer Beetz Brothers Hail Skydance For Backing Casey Bloys: "A Strong Sign The HBO Line Will Continue" News 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 Star Taissa Farmiga Talks Gladys' "Intense" First Episode The show performed well on The CW and HBO Max in the U.S. It has already gone to countries around the world including SBS in Australia, NRK in Norway, SVT in Sweden, DR in Denmark, YLE in Finland, RUV in Iceland and Amediateka in the CIS region. Watch on Deadline Sherlock & Daughter was created, written and executive produced by Brendan Foley. The Closer alum James Duff is showrunner, joined by writer Shelly Goldstein and writer/consultant Micah War Dog Wright. It is produced by Starlings UK affiliate Albion Television and its co-producing partner StoryFirst, together with financiers Krempelwood and MBM3. “It’s an honor to bring a show that has become such an international hit home to HBO Max in the UK and Ireland – both the home of its setting and where it was made in Dublin and London by a fantastic cast and crew, led by mighty performances from David Thewlis, Dougray Scott and Blu Hunt,” Foley said. “In these bumpy times, we’re very proud it has appealed so widely across generations worldwide, from new younger followers to veteran fans of the world’s greatest detective.” Ahead of the UK premiere and off the back of the latest distribution deals, Starlings CEO Karine Martin said: “Sherlock Holmes may belong to London but it took a global audience to make this homecoming truly extraordinary. title: UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars View All November 3, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source David Walliams Merlin Entertainments The World of David Walliams , an attraction at British theme park Alton Towers, is shutting up shop. The Merlin Entertainments-owned park said it would permanently close the Walliams-themed attraction after it opened in 2021, bringing to life characters from his books, such as Gangsta Granny. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Oscars: Every Best Picture Winner Back To The Beginning In 1929 A Merlin Entertainments spokesperson told Deadline: “As the 2026 peak season at Alton Towers Resort comes to an end and following our regular review of rides and attractions across the resort, we have taken the decision to permanently close the World of David Walliams.” Merlin Entertainments did not elaborate, but it is understood that the company took a range of operational and guest experience factors into consideration. Walliams’ literary agent at Independent Talent has been approached for comment. Watch on Deadline The closure follows Walliams’ publisher, HarperCollins, dropping the author and halting the publication of his back catalog following misconduct allegations. Walliams strongly denied wrongdoing after accusations about his behavior were published in The Daily Telegraph last year. Separately, Deadline revealed in September that YMU is no longer actively representing the comedian and his profile has been removed from the agency’s website. A source said Walliams “is not currently in a commercial relationship with YMU” following amicable talks in early 2026. Walliams is an established presence on British television and beyond, having created and co-starred in Little Britain with Matt Lucas in the noughties. They have made attempts to revive the BBC comedy and even spoke to Netflix about a new series in 2020. Walliams has appeared in series, including Doctor Who and Agatha Christie adaptation Partners in Crime , and had roles in movies including Murder Mystery and Stardust . He served as a judge on Britain’s Got Talent for a decade alongside Simon Cowell, but left the show under a cloud after comments he made about contestants were leaked to The Guardian in 2022. In one example, he called someone a “c***.” Walliams later apologized for his comments.
